question: A balance was 235 dollars. In the morning, 197 were spent. By midday, 45 were recovered. By afternoon, 64 were removed. By evening, the remaining multiplied by 6 and was converted to 6-dollar units (unit conversion). How many final units?

A student had 56 pages. They divided in half to 28. They divided in half again to 14. They multiplied by 5 to 70. They added 9, reaching 79. They multiplied by 4 to 316 pages. Converting to reading time was separate. How many pages total?

Dmitri's bakery had 132 sacks of flour in the store, and the mill sent 14 more. Each sack fills 5 trays of dough, and every tray is cut into 8 rolls. A neighbour then donated 25 baked rolls to the shop. Dmitri has more rolls this week than his rival Ana does, and his oven takes 40 minutes to heat up. How many rolls does Dmitri have?

A relief group had 153 blankets in each of its warehouses, and a donor tripled the number in every warehouse. Then 136 blankets were handed out from each warehouse during the cold snap. The group has 7 warehouses, all stocked and used identically. A school then collected 36 blankets and a church collected 65, and both lots were added to the group's total. How many blankets does the relief group have now?
A student had 23 pages morning. Removed 3 pages. Divided by 2 for reading. Removed 3 more. Removed 2 more pages. Converting to reading hours, how many hours?

A store started with 160 items. In the morning, the count multiplied by 8. By afternoon, the inventory was split into 5 equal departments. Then 103 items were sold. By evening, 71 items arrived. What was the final inventory count?

Priya kept a single jar of glass marbles that held 238 marbles one Saturday morning. During a game with friends she won 33 more marbles, then found 21 additional ones under the porch. At lunch, her little brother borrowed a dozen cookies from the pantry for a snack, which had nothing to do with the marbles, but Priya still had to pay back 253 marbles she owed her cousin from an old bet. That afternoon, a marble-trading event that took two hours, or 120 minutes, to organize turned every marble she had into 6 new ones, and later a bonus round turned each of those into 9 more. Finally, she gave 128 marbles to her cousin as a thank-you gift. How many marbles did Priya have in her jar after giving the thank-you gift?

Early one morning Ana counted 196 sacks of rice in the relief depot, and every sack holds 9 bags. In the late morning her colleague Bruno, who counts more slowly than Ana does, weighed the bags and found that each bag fills 8 cups. During the afternoon the kitchen staff measured that each cup of rice fills 4 small bowls. In the evening the head cook worked out that each bowl feeds 5 children at the shelter. How many children can the depot's rice feed?

Devon started the month with 128 minutes on his music-practice card. He used 119 minutes preparing for an audition, then his teacher added 29 minutes as a reward and his aunt bought him 62 more. He divided the minutes then on the card equally into 5 identical daily slots and kept just one slot on his own card, passing the rest to his sister. A rescan glitch cost him 2 minutes, and the studio credited him 46 minutes for a lesson it cancelled. The studio prints these credits in hours on its noticeboard, but Devon always counts his in minutes, and half of the practice rooms were closed for painting that week. How many minutes are on Devon's card now?

A wholesaler sells snack bars for 20 cents each. There are 6 bars in a pack, 3 packs in a box, and 5 boxes in a crate, so one crate of bars costs eighteen dollars before delivery. The wholesaler adds 17 cents to the price of each crate for delivery. A shop orders 7 crates. How many cents does the shop pay?

A warehouse had 186 boxes initially. They removed 153 through shipment. Then 7 more were removed. Finally, 14 more departed. The remaining multiplied by 7 for next order, converting to work-hours projected. A distribution center had 1000 boxes but separate. How many work-hours for next order?

In the morning a grocer had 233 tomatoes, and 67 of them were too soft to sell. He shared the rest equally between his 2 stalls. In the afternoon the worker at the first stall cut every tomato there into 4 slices. In the evening every slice from that stall was sold for 2 cents. How many cents did the first stall take from the slices?

On Monday morning a workshop counted 221 rolls of wire in the store, and every roll measures 8 metres. During the afternoon the team cut each metre into 7 short pieces. In the early evening every piece was bent into 2 hooks, and each hook was then dipped 6 times into the paint tank. The paint tank was installed 3 years ago. How many dips into the paint tank were made?

A moving crew starts the day with 128 boxes loaded in a truck. At the first stop, 114 boxes are unloaded. A second pickup adds 62 more boxes. At the next stop, 25 boxes are unloaded. Another stop removes 22 more boxes, a stop that takes 30 minutes, or half an hour. Finally, a merge with a second truck multiplies the remaining boxes by 4. How many boxes are on the truck now?

A company started with 228 projects. They multiplied by 3 through team expansion. They added 65 projects from client requests. They subtracted 587 projects from scope reduction. They subtracted 93 projects from budget constraints. They multiplied by 9 for resource allocation. They multiplied by 7 for annual planning (measured in annual resource units). Michael and Sarah compared project loads across departments. Her colleague managed 32 projects separately. What was the annual resource requirement?

A candle shop had 47 candles in stock, tracked over 60 minutes, or 1 hour, of the morning. Six more matching shipments made the total seven times as large. A late delivery added 79 more candles. A big sale sold 129 candles. A donation added 38 more. Three more matching shipments made the total four times as large. Finally, the stock was split evenly across 4 storerooms, and only one storeroom's candles were counted. How many candles were in that storeroom at the end?

Mrs Patel bought 19 tomato seedlings for her balcony. She gave 17 of them to the community garden. The 2 seedlings she kept were shared equally between 2 identical pots, and she watched only the pot on the left. By July the plant in that pot had grown 3 tomatoes. She picked 2 of them for a salad. The balcony gets 6 hours of sun a day. How many tomatoes are still on that plant?

A store started with 74 items. They subtracted 44 items sold. They doubled the remainder. They added 13 items from restocking. Finally, 16 items were added. Using the word 'double', between Michael (morning) and Patricia (evening), with minutes-to-hours conversion, how many items total?

Alex had 100 marbles. His neighbor Ben had 80 marbles. Alex found 17 more marbles. His collection was multiplied by 5 in a trade. It was multiplied by 9 in another deal. It was multiplied by 6 in a final transaction. How many marbles does Alex have?
A collector had 92 items. They added 21 items. They added 56 items. They doubled them. They removed 328 items. David had fewer items. Maria had more. The total progressed. How many items?

A stationery depot opened the morning with 171 cartons of sticker sheets and sent 123 of them out on the early van. Each carton left on the floor contains 9 packs. At midday a supplier dropped off 11 loose packs to join them. Every single pack, old or new, holds 8 sheets, and each sheet carries 9 stickers. In the evening a customer returned 32 individual stickers still on their backing, and the owner, who has run the depot for a dozen years, wanted the full count. How many stickers does the depot hold in total?

A council nursery had 118 trays of saplings, and 69 trays went out to the parks. A donation added 39 trays. Each tray was then split into 3 pots, and every pot was later divided into 6 seedlings. Storm damage killed 558 seedlings, and 299 were given away on community planting day. The nursery has 14 greenhouses, and it measures growth in centimetres although its reports are written in metres. How many seedlings are left?

A toy store started with 27 figures in stock. In February inventory tripled to 81 figures. In March it multiplied by 8 more. The store restocked 37 additional figures. By year-end seasonal sales multiplied the total fivefold. The store's competitor had 89 figures. How many figures did the toy store have by year-end?

A business had 166 dollars. They added 73 dollars. They removed 80 dollars. They removed 66 dollars. They removed 37 dollars. The time was minutes to hours. Morning transactions, afternoon deposits, evening totals. The money progressed. How much money?

The courier depot loaded 120 parcels into its bay at the start of the day, and it quotes delivery windows in minutes rather than in hours. The parcels were split equally among the 4 rounds, and the supervisor followed the van doing the morning round. That driver collected 73 further parcels from a business park. She then delivered 29 parcels along the ring road. A second pick-up put 66 more parcels into her van. Before returning she delivered 116 parcels around the housing estate. How many parcels were still in her van?
